source.title: Visualizing the Loss Landscape of Winning Lottery Tickets

record.tranche_reason: Measures loss-landscape flatness and sharpness against generalization-related outcomes and argues that the previously claimed correlation does not hold consistently; also reports batch-size and pruning comparisons relevant to the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures loss landscapes and reports performance outcomes for batch-size and pruning experiments. Figure-specific numeric values are not recoverable from the supplied text, so only explicitly stated outcomes are recorded. Results cited from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures projected held-out loss geometry and test performance, not V7's magnitude-aware tolerance before training error rises or its relationship to the train–test gap among similarly fitted networks. Its batch-size experiment does not establish V5's fixed epoch budget. These related results therefore do not directly test a supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: their filter-wise normalized visualizations fail to consistently associate flatness or sharpness with generalization performance in the batch-size and pruning experiments. They tentatively suggest that projected convexity remains associated with trainability and test performance when minima are sufficiently deep.
record.recipe_differences: Uses filter-wise normalized random-direction loss-landscape projections rather than magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance; pruning experiments compare IMP tickets with random masks.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes the reported landscape shape; pruning method changes landscape and performance comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: IMP tickets retain comparable test accuracy while their projected landscapes become flatter and shallower. Random tickets become flatter yet perform worse; Section 7 reports a final test-accuracy disadvantage of 16 percentage points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Flatness in filter-wise normalized two-dimensional projections of held-out loss does not consistently rank test accuracy across pruning methods and sparsities.

fits_no_version.finding: For LeNet5 with dropout and batch normalization trained using Adam on Fashion-MNIST, the best reported performance occurs at batch sizes between 160 and 1,600. Projected landscapes sharpen and deepen with increasing batch size before becoming flatter and shallower again.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size can affect test performance and projected loss geometry nonmonotonically; projected flatness need not indicate better test performance.

record.problems: The supplied text does not give numerical outcomes for the figure-based comparisons, error bars, or statistical tests. The paper says loss-landscape projections failed to correlate with generalization error, but the supplied text does not detail the two comparisons behind that statement.
record.rows_left_out: No separate batch-size rows were extracted: the text describes the loss-surface trend and says best performance lies between batch sizes 160 and 1,600, but does not report per-batch held-out performance values or specify a fixed epoch budget. Figure 4 values are figure-only.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under an established fixed epoch budget, and recipe adaptations that remove penalties.
Controlled dropout effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance measured using training error; correlation with train–test gaps among similarly fitted networks; comparison against norm and margin measures.
Removing memorized training examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Filter-wise normalization uses filter magnitudes, but this alone does not make projected held-out loss geometry equivalent to V7's magnitude-aware training-error tolerance. The authors' broader language about generalization does not establish the specific generalization-gap comparison V7 names. The batch-size findings are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels versus natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
The batch-size sweep is reported as a loss-landscape experiment, but the text does not give separate held-out performance values by batch size or establish a fixed epoch budget.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures are not tested; measurements use filter-wise normalized random directions and include lottery-ticket comparisons.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: LeNet5
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR10; best models obtained using early stopping
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss-landscape projections across iterative magnitude-pruning stages.

conditions.value: 10% of remaining weights every 35 epochs; 35 iterations; ending with only 3% of weights intact

rows.measure: Loss-landscape flatness and shallowness alongside test accuracy/generalization.
rows.value: The tickets perform comparably yet the landscapes get flatter and shallower as pruning continues.
rows.note: The text does not provide separate numeric test accuracies for these stages. The reported co-movement does not establish the version's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
rows.check: Comparable test accuracy alongside flatter projected test-loss landscapes does not measure V7's perturbation tolerance or generalization gap. The reported partial state is unsupported for V7.

rows.subject: LeNet5 random lottery tickets
rows.operation_detail: Compared random-mask ticket loss-landscape projections and performance with winning tickets produced by iterative magnitude pruning.
rows.measure: Loss-landscape flatness/shallow curvature and test performance.
rows.baseline: Winning tickets obtained using IMP; numeric baseline not stated.
rows.value: Random tickets perform much worse relative to the WLTs and are vastly more shallow.
rows.note: The text explicitly associates flatness and shallowness in these projections with poor generalization, but gives no numerical values for this comparison.
rows.check: Random tickets have flatter, shallower projected test-loss landscapes and worse test accuracy, but training fit and generalization gaps are not established. Section 7 also reports a final test-accuracy difference of 16 percentage points, omitted from this row's value.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: LeNet5 lottery-ticket pruning comparisons on CIFAR10
reader_labels.reason: The reported geometry and performance comparisons are consistent with a relationship in this setting, but use filter-wise normalized projections rather than magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance (R1, R2). The paper also states that its visualizations have twice failed to correlate flatness or sharpness with generalization error.
